parts.label: FRONT CLAMP
parts.desc: Band clamp holding the hose on the front block's nozzle.

parts.label: REAR SOCKET
parts.desc: Ring socket where the hose enters the lower shell near the breech.

parts.label: COOLANT HOSE
parts.desc: Ribbed silver coolant hose. It leaves the front block, loops down and back in a U under the body and enters the lower shell near the breech.

parts.label: FRONT BLOCK
parts.desc: Chunky stepped gunmetal block bolted under the front shroud: the coolant manifold where the ribbed hose starts its loop back to the breech.

parts.label: FRONT SHROUD
parts.desc: Thick rust-brown front shroud, faceted like the 1997 original and ringed by a dark seam. Its recessed slot is the rail exit: the slug leaves here at hypersonic speed.

parts.label: BUTT PLATE
parts.desc: Flat angular butt plate, tilted back. The shoulder takes the recoil of a slug fired at rail speed.

parts.label: LEFT STOCK ROD
parts.desc: One of the two thin parallel stock rods that carry the butt plate.

parts.label: RIGHT STOCK ROD
parts.desc: The second stock rod, side by side with the first.

parts.label: LEFT COVER
parts.desc: Left side plate of the rear housing, bolted and riveted over the breech electronics.

parts.label: RIGHT COVER
parts.desc: Right side plate of the rear housing.

parts.label: TRIGGER
parts.desc: Slanted trigger blade and guard under the rear housing. One pull dumps the whole capacitor bank into the rails.

parts.label: REAR HOUSING
parts.desc: Faceted gunmetal breech block behind the body: takes the recoil, holds the trigger and anchors the two stock rods.

parts.label: STATUS LAMPS
parts.desc: Two small round orange-red status lamps on the left flank at the front of the panel: idle glow, flare on charge.

parts.label: PANEL BEZEL
parts.desc: Raised gunmetal frame around the circuit panel window, screwed to the upper shell, with the dark lamp plate below its front end.

parts.label: CIRCUIT PANEL
parts.desc: The red charge-control board set into the top of the body. Its traces glow orange as the coils charge, the railgun's only readout.

parts.label: UPPER SHELL
parts.desc: Upper half of the faceted main body: rusty brown paint over bronze, milled with the window that holds the circuit panel.

parts.label: LOWER SHELL
parts.desc: Lower half of the main body. Carries the hose socket near the breech and shields the capacitor bank.

parts.label: HEAT SINK
parts.desc: Finned heat sink under the upper shell; bleeds coil heat into the coolant loop.

parts.label: CAPACITOR BANK
parts.desc: Four banded capacitors and a copper bus bar: they store the charge for one shot.

parts.label: POWER CELL
parts.desc: Cell with a window onto its glowing orange core; recharges the capacitor bank between shots.

parts.label: SLUG MAGAZINE
parts.desc: Feed box with the depleted-uranium slugs, one chambered per shot.

parts.label: DU SLUG
parts.desc: The chambered depleted-uranium slug. It leaves the muzzle faster than sound can follow.

parts.label: COIL 6
parts.desc: Accelerator coil 6 of 6: copper windings on a bobbin around the bore. They fire in sequence from the breech to the muzzle.

parts.label: COIL 5
parts.desc: Accelerator coil 5 of 6: copper windings on a bobbin around the bore. They fire in sequence from the breech to the muzzle.

parts.label: COIL 4
parts.desc: Accelerator coil 4 of 6: copper windings on a bobbin around the bore. They fire in sequence from the breech to the muzzle.

parts.label: COIL 3
parts.desc: Accelerator coil 3 of 6: copper windings on a bobbin around the bore. They fire in sequence from the breech to the muzzle.

parts.label: COIL 2
parts.desc: Accelerator coil 2 of 6: copper windings on a bobbin around the bore. They fire in sequence from the breech to the muzzle.

parts.label: COIL 1
parts.desc: Accelerator coil 1 of 6: copper windings on a bobbin around the bore. They fire in sequence from the breech to the muzzle.

parts.label: CONDUCTOR RAILS
parts.desc: Two parallel copper rails inside the bore. The current loop between them throws the slug.

parts.label: BORE TUBE
parts.desc: Inner barrel liner: the fixed spine of the gun that everything else is built around.
